prompt: Write the checks that tell a correct linear search apart from three broken ones. Complete isCorrect in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Each bug hides behind a different input, and no single call reveals more than one of them: a present, unique target is answered correctly by all three broken searchers. The missing target exercises the failure path, an array with the value at two positions pins down FIRST rather than last, and the empty array is the boundary where a do-while loop reads element 0 that is not there. Deciding what the method must do in each of those situations before writing code is exactly what a test suite records.
hints: indexOf({4, 7, 9}, 7) == 1 is true for every implementation in this exercise, including the broken ones -- it cannot be your only check.
Add a call where the target is ABSENT (expect -1) and one where the target appears twice (expect the FIRST index).
Pass new int[] {} as well, and wrap everything in try/catch returning false: one implementation reads element 0 of the empty array.
